overview: New Talisman Gold Mines Limited is a New Zealand-incorporated, NZX-listed gold and silver explorer transitioning toward small-scale production at its wholly owned Talisman project in the historic Karangahake goldfield (Coromandel/Hauraki), between Waihi and Paeroa. The company holds a 25-year Minerals Mining Permit (51326, granted 2009) covering the former Talisman and Crown-Welcome mines plus the adjoining Rahu exploration permit, and reports a JORC (2012) mineral resource of approximately 350,000 ounces of gold-equivalent at an average grade of ~17 g/t. During FY2026 it commissioned a gravity-separation processing plant and produced first gold concentrate, but production volumes have not been sufficient to generate positive cash flow, leaving the company reliant on repeated equity raisings and formally in going-concern/audit-disclaimer territory.

business_model.summary: Pre-commercial narrow-vein underground gold/silver miner monetizing ore via toll processing and concentrate offtake rather than owning a full smelting/refining chain. Revenue is nascent, volatile, and currently immaterial relative to costs (FY2026 operating income NZ$52,790 vs. operating + admin expenses of ~NZ$2.27m); the company has never reported a sustained profitable operating year and funds itself primarily through share issuance.

revenue_streams.name: Gold/silver concentrate sales (Ocean Partners UK, 100% offtake)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - two offtake/processing counterparties (Ocean Partners UK for concentrate, Melody Gold for low-grade ore/tailings); effectively a two-customer concentration risk
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand (Coromandel Peninsula/Hauraki Goldfield); no international operations

main_competitors: Other ASX/TSX-V junior NZ gold explorers
competitive_position.market_position: Sub-scale, pre-commercial junior explorer/emerging producer; market cap roughly NZ$9-15m versus OceanaGold's multi-billion dollar, cash-flow-positive Waihi operation a few kilometres away. No meaningful market share of NZ gold output.

moat_factors.description: 25-year Minerals Mining Permit (51326) granted 2009 over 299 hectares including historic Talisman and Crown-Welcome workings, plus adjoining Rahu exploration permit (5-year term, renewable) - provides secured tenure and optionality without needing to win a new permit

Karangahake deposit has ~1 million oz gold / 3 million oz silver of historical production (1880s-1992) at high grades (resource averages ~17 g/t, with Dubbo zone at 21.6 g/t and Mystery inferred at 25 g/t), which is genuinely attractive rock if it can be mined economically
Company has existing underground workings, a commissioned processing plant, and offtake agreements already in place rather than starting from a greenfield site

No cost advantage, no brand recognition, no economies of scale versus larger regional operators; narrow-vein epithermal mining is inherently higher-cost and lower-margin than the bulk/open-pit or larger underground operations of peers

weaknesses: Single asset (Talisman project) with no producing diversification - total dependence on one narrow-vein orebody

Narrow-vein (approx. 1m width) epithermal mining creates high grade variability and unpredictable vein orientation, directly causing FY2026's development delays and lower-than-planned concentrate grade
No demonstrated ability to mine and process at a rate that generates positive cash flow after four-plus years of trying
Micro-cap scale (market cap roughly NZ$9-15m) limits access to capital markets and institutional investor interest
History of going-concern qualifications and audit disclaimers of opinion in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 - a severe, repeated red flag
ASX secondary listing suspended in June 2024 due to inadequate financial condition, cutting off that capital-raising channel

growth_drivers: Conversion of inferred resource (330,000 oz, ~94% of the total 350,000 oz resource) to indicated/measured categories via 3D geological modelling and targeted drilling, which would materially de-risk mine planning

Resource expansion drilling at Mystery, Dubbo, Crown/Welcome and the new Rahu exploration permit (granted December 2024, 387 hectares directly north of the Talisman permit, viewed as the northern extension of the Karangahake mineralised corridor)
Opening of additional production faces (e.g., rehabilitation at Dubbo) to reduce single-face dependency and support scalable output

Ramp-up of the newly commissioned processing plant and utilisation of the Ocean Partners (concentrate) and Melody Gold (low-grade ore/tailings) offtake agreements to convert mined material into cash flow
Supportive gold price environment (spot gold near record highs through 2025-2026, with some forecasts of USD ~$4,900/oz by end-2026) improving project economics if production can be scaled

business.description: Entire company value is tied to the Talisman project; any negative geological, permitting, or operational development is existential

FY2026 mining at Mystery vein demonstrated 'the complexities of predicting the orebody orientation' from short-scale geological variability; only ~10m of reef drivage mined to date against forecast assumptions that were not met, and first concentrate shipment realised a lower grade than planned
Revenue depends on two counterparties (Ocean Partners UK for 100% of concentrate, Melody Gold for low-grade ore/tailings)
Company states plainly that 'initial production levels were not sufficient to sustain positive cash flows' - the core operating thesis is not yet validated

financial.description: H1 FY2026 filing states the company 'currently has a low cash balance in relation to its usual cash demand which makes going concern a risk'; FY2026 year-end cash was only ~NZ$1.18m against ongoing negative operating cash flow (~NZ$2.0m used in FY2026)

Shares on issue grew from ~625m (Sep 2024) to ~679m (Sep 2025) to ~793m (March 2026) via repeated placements and a 4-for-5 rights issue at NZ$0.016/share (March 2026); the company has raised nearly all of its funding history through equity issuance rather than debt or operating cash flow

Management states explicitly that 'further capital will be required to fully implement all phases' of the strategic plan, and that 'no assurance can be given that such capital will be available at all or on terms acceptable to the Company'

regulatory.description: Baker Tilly Staples Rodway issued a disclaimer of opinion (not just a qualified opinion) on the FY2026 accounts, unable to obtain sufficient evidence on the recoverable amount of the ~NZ$15.6m Talisman Mine cash-generating unit; the FY2025 accounts also received a disclaimer, and FY2024 accounts (per prior auditor) likewise could not be opined on - a persistent, multi-year pattern

ASX secondary listing was suspended in June 2024 because ASX determined the company's financial condition was 'not adequate to warrant continued quotation,' removing a capital-raising and liquidity avenue (NZX primary listing continues, with periodic NZX trading halts around material announcements)

Provision for closure and rehabilitation (~NZ$452,599 at March 2026) reflects ongoing obligations under NZ environmental law and Department of Conservation access arrangements; a $100,000 bond is held on DOC's behalf

macro.description: Project economics and resource cut-off grades are directly tied to gold (and silver) prices; while spot gold has been strong through 2025-2026, a price pullback would further pressure already-marginal production economics
Mining and processing costs, plus offtake proceeds, carry some currency and commodity cost exposure typical of small NZ resource companies

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold prices have been strong through 2025-2026, with some bank forecasts calling for USD gold near $4,900/oz by end-2026, which is broadly supportive for gold project economics globally, including in New Zealand's Hauraki Goldfield where OceanaGold continues to invest in and extend the nearby Waihi operation
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - junior gold explorer/emerging producer economics are acutely sensitive to gold price cycles and to the company's own binary operational execution risk (whether it can mine and process at a rate that generates positive cash flow)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful - lower global interest rates typically support gold prices and improve junior miners' access to capital; NTL's heavy reliance on equity capital markets also makes it sensitive to risk-on/risk-off sentiment toward speculative micro-caps
key_input_costs: Labour and contractor costs for underground development
Consumables for the gravity separation plant

recent_developments.event: Entered Business Confirmation with Ocean Partners UK (29 Oct 2025) for gold concentrate sale; NZ RegCo trading halt applied around this announcement

Board/management turnover: Terry Moynihan appointed independent non-executive director (3 Nov 2025); John Upperton resigned from Board and management roles (14 Nov 2025); Jane Bell appointed interim General Manager (17 Nov 2025)
First shipment of gold concentrate announced as imminent, but grade of the concentrate was lower than planned, realising only US$21.7k
Company sought and was granted a further NZX trading halt
Completed a pro-rata renounceable 4-for-5 rights issue at NZ$0.016/share, raising approximately NZ$1.3m in total (including shortfall placement of NZ$27,842), lifting shares on issue to ~793.3m
Long-serving independent director Michael Stiassny retired from the Board

FY2026 annual report released with a disclaimer of audit opinion (Baker Tilly Staples Rodway) on the Talisman Mine cash-generating unit's recoverable amount, and disclosure that initial production was insufficient to sustain positive cash flow, prompting a strategic reset toward drilling/geological modelling before resuming development
AGM scheduled for 16 September 2026; company continuing to evaluate further funding options to implement its revised strategic plan

items.target: Pause further mine development in favour of geological modelling, targeted drilling, and rehabilitation; recommence development on a 'more informed and efficient basis'
items.notes: No quantitative production, revenue, or cash flow targets have been disclosed; guidance is qualitative and centred on de-risking the resource before scaling output

items.target: Additional capital required beyond the ~NZ$1.3m rights offer to fully implement all phases of the strategic plan
items.notes: No specific amount or timing disclosed; Board says it 'continues to evaluate funding options and prioritisation of activities'

items.target: Drilling at Mystery, Dubbo, Crown/Welcome and Rahu to convert inferred resources to indicated/measured and expand the resource base
items.vs_prior: new/expanded scope vs prior single-mine focus
items.notes: Approximately 1,000m of diamond drilling assumed at Dubbo subject to detailed planning; no resource-growth target ounces given

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Samantha Sharif: 'While there is still considerable work ahead, we believe the Company is now better positioned, with a clearer plan, stronger technical foundation, and improved commercial arrangements... We remain committed to unlocking the full potential of the Talisman project and delivering long-term value.' No quantitative revenue, margin, or production guidance has been issued for FY2027; management explicitly frames the near-term focus as risk reduction (geology/drilling) rather than production ramp-up.

bull_case: Large in-situ resource (350,000 oz gold-equivalent at ~17 g/t) in a historically rich goldfield (Karangahake, part of the Hauraki Goldfield that also hosts OceanaGold's profitable Waihi mine) offers optionality if grade/continuity risk can be resolved

Processing plant is now commissioned and commercial offtake agreements (Ocean Partners UK for concentrate, Melody Gold for low-grade ore/tailings) are in place, removing two historical bottlenecks (no processing capability, no buyer) and creating at least the mechanical pathway to revenue
Strong gold price environment through 2025-2026 improves the economics of any incremental ounce produced and could ease future capital raising if the operational thesis is proven out
Additional exploration upside at Rahu (newly granted permit, viewed as northern extension of the Karangahake structural corridor) and at Crown/Welcome beyond the current 350,000 oz resource base

Refreshed technical leadership (new mining-experienced directors such as Terry Moynihan) and a more disciplined, staged strategic plan focused on de-risking via drilling before further capital-intensive development
bear_case: Two consecutive years (at least) of disclaimer-of-opinion audits is a severe red flag - auditors could not even form a view on whether the company's largest asset (~NZ$15.6m Talisman Mine CGU, the vast majority of the balance sheet) is recoverable

Going-concern language is explicit and unresolved: the company has 'a low cash balance in relation to its usual cash demand,' FY2026 year-end cash of only ~NZ$1.18m, and forecasts depend on production/grade assumptions that management itself says have already not been met once

Extreme and ongoing shareholder dilution - shares on issue nearly doubled from FY2024 levels (roughly 625m to ~793m by March 2026) purely to fund cash burn, with no offsetting operating cash generation, and management has flagged that even more capital will be needed

Operational execution has repeatedly disappointed: narrow-vein mining proved harder to predict than planned, the first concentrate shipment realised a lower grade than expected (only US$21.7k), and development at Mystery had to be paused entirely

ASX suspension (June 2024) for inadequate financial condition, a near-nil operating history of profitability, and a market cap of only roughly NZ$9-15m leave the stock with very thin liquidity, minimal institutional interest, and high binary risk of further capital destruction if the strategic reset does not deliver sustainable positive cash flow
